motif.variation: rhythmic diminution in A' (p1:5/p1:6 halve every value), two-row displacement in p1:3, and re-harmonisation under the bVI chromatic mediant in p1:6 and p1:11

qa.notes: POLYMETER (structural, and it is the piece's argument): the B section's written-out ostinato is a FIVE-ROW broken-chord cell laid straight across a 16-row bar (pulse 1, frames 8-11, p1:7-p1:10) — 5 against 4, accented on every cell head (vol 13 vs 10), so it never lines up with the barline inside a frame and the chord changes cut across it mid-cell. That is the contrast the brief asks for: pulse 2's 0xy bed in A is an arpeggio EFFECT locked to the bar, pulse 1's B ostinato is an arpeggio WRITTEN OUT and deliberately out of phase with it. Second polyrhythm: the A bed pulses 3+3+2 (tresillo) inside every bar — strikes at rows 0/6/12 with Sxx chokes at 5/11/15 — so the harmony breathes instead of droning (p2:2, p2:3). Third: A' puts a 3-row walking-bass cell on the triangle (frames 6-7, tri:4/tri:5, notes every 3 rows across the bar) under an 8th-note bed, and the A' hats carry a 6-row accent cycle (vol 9 every 3rd hat) against 4/4. METRIC EVENT: frame 11 rows 48-63 go half-time — the ostinato halves to 8ths under an Axy fade and the kit drops to one hit a beat — before A'' snaps back. MOTIF: stated in p1:1, displaced two rows in p1:3, and put through rhythmic DIMINUTION in A' (p1:5/p1:6 halve every value so the 4-bar phrase fits in 2). HARMONY: A climbs I-ii-iii-IV then V-vi-IV-V, each phrase entering a step higher; B arrives on F#m through C#7 (V/vi, the e sharp is the colour) and then chains G#7 -> C#7 -> F#m (frames 10-11); A' and A'' both use F major, the bVI chromatic mediant, against A major (frames 7 and 14). WRITTEN DISSONANCES (section 9.2 quota), two, both genuinely prepared: (1) cadential 4-3 over the dominant - pulse 2 attacks f sharp 4 (66) at 8:44 as the fifth of the B minor bar, holds it THROUGH the change to C#7 at 8:48 where it is the fourth, and resolves down by step to e sharp 4 (65) at 8:52, C#7's third, which then rises to f sharp 4 at 8:56 for the cadential arrival on F#m at 9:0; (2) flat-9 suspension under the chromatic mediant - the A' bed attacks f4 (65) at 7:28 as the root of the bVI F major, the harmony turns back to E at 7:32 with the f held through the change as a minor ninth above the root, and it resolves down by step to e4 at 7:36. The Sxx chokes at 7:31 and 7:35 are deliberately absent so that suspension can sound; every other bed strike keeps its choke. DECIMAL PARAMS: 0 param 71 = 047 major triad, 55 = 037 minor, 74 = 04a dominant 7, 0 = cancel; S param 4/5 = a cut 4 or 5 ticks into a 7-tick row; V param 0/2 = duty 12.5% / 50%; A param 3 = A03 swell UP (inverted convention), 32 = A20 fade. Vxx is INERT against every bank instrument here because their duty macros overwrite it on the next tick, so the ostinato runs on x-glass-ladder-glass, a vol-pluck instrument with NO duty macro, which is the only way Vxx can speak; the loop-target frame reinstates pulse 1 as lead-bright, whose duty macro overrides any stale Vxx state. The suite-wide rmsRange convention: the measured two-pass mix RMS +-1.5 dB, declared per song because the design's [-20,-9] window is unreachable on this engine and the floor is -30 dBFS. Measured -21.07 dBFS, declared [-22.57, -19.57]. DENSITY (9.8): every bar is at or under 28 attacks across all five lanes, peak 28 (it was 33 at 14:32 across 18 of 64 bars). Under a 16-attack written-out ostinato the kit thins rather than the ostinato: in B the closed hats move to the off-8ths only (rows 2/6/10/14 of each bar) and the ghost snares come out, and in A'' the hats leave the returning ostinato bare from 14:32 - both are section-level kit variations of the kind 9.4 asks for. Accidentals 6.5%.
